purpose: Determine which central-bank-specific reaction-function hypotheses can be tested with currently certified point-in-time data without revised-history substitution or proxy leakage.
principles: Do not compare banks using different data-quality standards.
Do not infer a direct labour channel for a price-stability-primary bank when the wage/inflation bridge is missing.
Do not infer a dual-mandate labour channel when historical PIT labour is unavailable.
Rates/front-end confirmation may be tested only where a same-basis historical rate series exists.
WITHHELD means no vote and no synthetic fallback.

FED.required_test: Labour direct + inflation direct -> Fed expectations/front-end -> USD
FED.blocker: Historical PIT labour is unavailable; a Fed-vs-ECB labour comparison would be methodologically invalid today.

ECB.required_test: Labour -> wages/services/domestic inflation -> ECB expectations/front-end -> EUR

BOE.required_test: Labour tightness -> wages/services inflation -> BoE/front-end -> GBP

BOC.required_test: Labour/slack direct -> BoC/front-end -> CAD, conditioned by inflation anchor
BOC.latest_assessment: CAD labour shows materially stronger medium-horizon OOS behaviour than EUR direct labour, but is not yet a full BoC reaction-function test without rates/inflation conditioning.

RBA.required_test: Labour/full-employment gap direct + inflation direct -> RBA/front-end -> AUD

SNB.required_test: Activity/labour -> inflation forecast -> SNB rates/FX channel -> CHF

BOJ.required_test: Labour tightness -> wages -> sustainable inflation -> BoJ/rates -> JPY

valid_cross_class_comparison_now.interpretation: Use CAD versus EUR only as a diagnostic class contrast, not as a substitute for Fed versus ECB.

priority_order: 1. Build USD historical PIT labour and US 2Y same-basis front-end history to unlock true Fed-vs-ECB comparison.
2. Build GBP wages/services PIT plus UK front-end history to test BoE mediated labour channel.
3. Add CAD front-end and inflation-conditioning layer to convert current CAD labour attribution into a true BoC reaction-function test.
4. Keep AUD/NZD/CHF/JPY WITHHELD until historical PIT/event-time requirements are met.
